It is absent whenever `build` runs without an explicit path argument, which is exactly the scaffolded default (`npm run build` -> `extension build`). verdict.reason:
Confirmed, not reporter error. I re-fetched https://extension.js.org/docs/commands/build and read the whole "Machine output with `--output json`" section plus the options table above it. The page states unconditionally: "A successful run prints a `status: \"built\"` frame. Its `value` carries the project path, built browsers, the resolved mode, and one summary per browser." There is no qualifier anywhere on the page, and the options table one screen earlier actively reinforces the wrong expectation by documenting `[path]` with default `process.cwd()` — a reader concludes the resolved cwd will appear as the project path. Nothing in docs/contracts/result-envelope.mdx marks any envelope field optional either (grep for optional/omit/absent/undefined/"only when" returns nothing), so the condition is documented nowhere.

I reproduced it from a clean scaffold, not from the reporter's directory: `extension create ext-a --template=init` (whose generated package.json ships exactly `"build": "extension build"`, no path argument — so this is the default scaffolded path, as claimed), then ran the build both ways. Without a path argument `value` has keys ['browsers','mode','summaries'] and no `projectPath` at all; with an explicit `./ext-a` the key is present. The key is not null — it is absent, so a consumer doing `value.projectPath` gets undefined with no signal.

Root cause in this repo matches: programs/extension/commands/build.ts:305 emits `ENVELOPE.ok('build','built',{projectPath: pathOrRemoteUrl, ...})`. When no path argument is passed, `pathOrRemoteUrl` is undefined and `JSON.stringify` drops the key entirely. Note the adjacent `mode` field has a deliberate `mode ?? 'production'` default with a comment saying the key must "survive the default invocation with no --mode flag" — projectPath got no equivalent treatment, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than intent.

Severity medium rather than high: the payload is otherwise correct and a caller always knows its own cwd, so the workaround is trivial once known — but it fails silently on the most common invocation, and the same unconditional "carries the project path" phrasing also appears on dev.mdx:201, start.mdx:134, and preview.mdx:120, so the doc fix likely needs to cover those pages too (I did not verify the other three commands at runtime; preview launches a browser and I killed it rather than let it run).

Cheapest fix is on the product side (default `projectPath` to the resolved cwd, mirroring `mode`); if the omission is intended, the build page must say the key is present only when a path argument is passed.
